messages:
matt: Quick one  our next-edge example fails on Vercel: "Cannot use import statement outside a module". Local node preview ok.

gina: That usually means the edge runtime pulled the CJS entry. Do we have conditional exports?

matt: We only had main/module/types. No exports map.

oliver: Add an exports map with an "edge" condition so Edge gets ESM. Eg: 
```json
"exports": {
  "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "import": "./dist/node-esm/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs"
}
```

gina: Also noticed some TypeScript consumers hit TS2769 after we changed some public params from any -> unknown. Overload inference broke.

matt: Oof. Which TS versions?

gina: Mainly <4.8 and older tsconfigs. Overloads + unknown are brittle. Two fixes: simplify overloads into a single generic or ship a compat d.ts via typesVersions for older compilers.

oliver: I prefer typesVersions so modern users get strict types and older projects get looser defs. Example mapping: 
```json
"typesVersions": {
  "<4.8": { "*": ["dist/types-compat/*"] },
  "*": { "*": ["dist/types/*"] }
}
```

matt: Also saw retries hang on Edge because AbortController semantics differ. We should guard globals and polyfill where needed.

gina: For onboarding, ship a tiny runtime-detect wrapper in examples that picks the correct build automatically. That avoids a lot of confusion.

oliver: Action items: Ill add exports + publish canary; Gina will prepare typesVersions + compat d.ts; Matt will add Vercel smoke test in CI.
